user.title: Connect a JSY-MK-194 module
user.description: Choose the serial port of the USB/TTL adapter and enter the module's CURRENT Modbus settings. A new module ships with ID 1 at 4800 baud. The integration reads the module to validate the connection.

data.device_id: Current Modbus ID of the module (1 on a new module)
data.name: Device name in Home Assistant

data_description.port: Ports are listed by their stable name (/dev/serial/by-id/...) when the system provides one. You can also type a path.

assign_id.title: Modbus ID of the module

channels.title: Channels
channels.description:
Name each channel after what it measures, and say what circuit its current sensor is clamped on.

The module measures a single voltage, normally line–neutral, and uses it for both channels. For a load fed line-to-line on a split-phase panel (240 V breaker, no neutral), choose "Line–line": voltage, power and energy of that channel are multiplied by 2.

data_description.channel_1_name: Used in the entity names, for example "Heat pump Power (signed)" instead of "Power 1 (signed)".
data_description.channel_1_circuit: Reset the energy counters of the channel before changing this setting, otherwise the energy statistics record a jump.

parameters.title: Parameter selection — {device_name}
parameters.description: Tick the values to expose as sensors in Home Assistant. The pre-ticked ones are the recommended set. The values behind the editable entities (energy counters, Modbus ID, baud rate) are always included.

error.cannot_connect: No answer from the module. Check the port, the Modbus ID, the baud rate and the wiring (TX/RX crossed, module powered).
error.module_not_found: jsy_modbusdecoder.py is missing from custom_components/ha_jsy/ or one of its imports failed (see the log).
error.id_in_use: This Modbus ID is already used by another configured JSY module.
error.id_write_failed: The new ID was written but the module does not answer with it. It may need a power cycle; power-cycle it and start again with the new ID as the current ID.

abort.already_configured: A JSY module with this Modbus ID is already configured.

init.title: JSY-MK-194 options
init.description:
How Home Assistant reaches the module, the channels, and which values are exposed as sensors.

The serial port, Modbus ID and baud rate entered here must be the ones the module ALREADY has: they are checked against the module, and nothing is written to it. To change the module's own Modbus ID or baud rate, use the "Modbus Device ID (Set)" and "Baud Rate (Set)" entities on the device page.

The values behind the editable entities are always included in the sensors.

data.device_id: Modbus ID the module currently has
data.baudrate: Baud rate the module currently uses
data.auto_relocate: Look for the module on other ports when it stops answering

data_description.auto_relocate: Only adapters of the same USB model as the one selected are probed.
data_description.channel_1_name: Used in the entity names, for example "Heat pump Power (signed)" instead of "Power 1 (signed)".
data_description.channel_1_circuit: Reset the energy counters of the channel before changing this setting, otherwise the energy statistics record a jump.

error.id_in_use: This Modbus ID is already used by another configured JSY module.
error.cannot_connect: The module does not answer with these settings, so nothing was changed. This screen only tells Home Assistant where the module is. To change the module's own Modbus ID or baud rate, use the "Modbus Device ID (Set)" and "Baud Rate (Set)" entities on the device page.

options.line_line: Line–line, split-phase — voltage, power and energy ×2 (e.g. 240 V)
